statement: Whenever minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r, the following holds. Let n = len(nums), mn = min{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }, and mx = max{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }. Then r is the least integer of the form p + (n - 1 - q) - c, where p and q are indices with 0 <= p < n, 0 <= q < n, nums[p] = mn, nums[q] = mx, and c = 1 if p > q and c = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, the evaluation of minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r; it does not fail (no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r, r >= 0.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r, r <= 2 * len(nums) - 3.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r, let n = len(nums), mn = min{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }, and mx = max{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }. Then r = 0 if and only if nums[0] = mn and nums[n-1] = mx.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r, r = 2 * n - 3.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums), mn = min{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }, and mx = max{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }. The input satisfies len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 100000, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000 for all i, mn < mx, nums[0] = mx, nums[n-1] = mn, and for every i with 1 <= i <= n-2, mn < nums[i] < mx.

statement: Whenever minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r and minimum_swaps(nums2) returns a result r2, r = r2.
preconditions: For two arrays nums and nums2, both satisfy len(x) >= 1, len(x) <= 100000, and 1 <= x[i] <= 100000 for all valid indices, and they have the same length n. Let p0(x) be the least index p with 0 <= p < n and x[p] = min{ x[i] | 0 <= i < n }, and let q0(x) be the greatest index q with 0 <= q < n and x[q] = max{ x[i] | 0 <= i < n }. Assume p0(nums) = p0(nums2) and q0(nums) = q0(nums2).

statement: Whenever minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r, let n = len(nums), mn = min{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }, and mx = max{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }. There exists an array b and a finite sequence of exactly r adjacent swaps (each swap exchanges two neighboring entries of the current array) that transforms nums into b, such that b[0] = mn and b[n-1] = mx.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r, let n = len(nums), mn = min{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }, and mx = max{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }. For every integer k with 0 <= k < r and every array b obtainable from nums by exactly k adjacent swaps, either b[0] != mn or b[n-1] != mx.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r, r = p0 + (n - 1 - q0).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums), mn = min{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }, mx = max{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }, p0 = the least index p with nums[p] = mn, and q0 = the greatest index q with nums[q] = mx. The input satisfies len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000 for all i, and p0 <= q0.

statement: Whenever minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r, r = p0 + (n - 1 - q0) - 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums), mn = min{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }, mx = max{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }, p0 = the least index p with nums[p] = mn, and q0 = the greatest index q with nums[q] = mx. The input satisfies len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000 for all i, and p0 > q0.

statement: Whenever minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r, r <= n - 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums), mn = min{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }, and mx = max{ nums[i] | 0 <= i < n }. The input satisfies len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000 for all i, and (nums[0] = mn or nums[n-1] = mx).

statement: Whenever minimum_swaps(nums) returns a result r, r = 0 if nums[0] <= nums[1], and r = 1 if nums[0] > nums[1].
